summary: The foundational systems language: direct memory pointers, structs, explicit allocations, and zero runtime overhead.

rows.means: preprocessor directive importing standard library header prototypes
rows.consequence: Copies the header declaration signatures into the file before compilation so the compiler knows function arguments and return types.

rows.means: macro text substitution and conditional compilation guards
rows.consequence: #ifndef HEADER_H prevents duplicate declaration errors when headers are included multiple times across compilation units.

rows.means: primitive numeric, character, and untyped data types
rows.consequence: Directly map to hardware register sizes: char is 1 byte, int is typically 4 bytes, double is 8-byte IEEE 754 floating point.

rows.means: variable holding the physical RAM memory address of another variable
rows.consequence: *ptr accesses the value stored at that address (dereferencing); &x extracts the hexadecimal memory address of variable x.

rows.means: allocates uninitialized heap memory / releases heap memory
rows.consequence: Every malloc must be paired with exactly one free. Forgetting free causes memory leaks; using ptr after free causes undefined behavior.

rows.means: allocates zeroed memory / resizes existing heap allocation
rows.consequence: calloc clears all bytes to zero; realloc resizes existing allocations, copying contents to a new memory block if necessary.

rows.code: struct User { int id; char name[32]; };
rows.means: contiguous composite data layout in memory
rows.consequence: Groups heterogeneous fields into a single struct. Access fields with dot (.) on values, or arrow (->) on pointers (user_ptr->id).

rows.means: creates an alias name for a type
rows.consequence: Allows referring to User_t directly without having to write struct User on every variable declaration.

rows.code: union Data { int i; float f; char str[20]; };
rows.means: shares the same memory location between multiple fields
rows.consequence: The union is only as large as its largest member. Writing to one field overwrites the data of all other fields.

rows.means: enumerated named integer constants
rows.consequence: Assigns sequential integers starting at 0 unless explicitly specified, making code more readable than raw magic numbers.

rows.code: const int x vs int * const ptr vs const int *ptr
rows.means: immutable value / constant pointer address / pointer to constant value
rows.consequence: Read backwards from right to left: const int *ptr is a pointer to constant integer (the data cannot be modified through this pointer).

rows.means: limits symbol visibility to the current file or preserves local state
rows.consequence: Inside a function, static preserves value across multiple calls; at file level, keeps functions and globals private.

rows.means: computes byte size at compile time
rows.consequence: Always use sizeof(*ptr) with malloc: malloc(sizeof(int) * count) guarantees correct byte allocation on any CPU architecture.

rows.means: formatted print to standard output
rows.consequence: %d formats signed integer, %s prints null-terminated char array, %p prints memory address in hexadecimal format.

rows.means: safely formats string into a fixed-size memory buffer
rows.consequence: Guarantees null termination and prevents catastrophic buffer overflow attacks that plague unsafe legacy sprintf().

rows.means: opens a file stream / flushes and closes the stream
rows.consequence: mode can be "r" (read), "w" (overwrite), "a" (append), or "rb" (binary). Always check if fp == NULL before reading.

rows.means: reads / writes raw binary data from or to a file stream
rows.consequence: Reads directly into memory buffers without string translation, essential for binary protocols, image processing, and databases.

rows.means: scans until null byte '\0' / returns allocated buffer size
rows.consequence: char str[10] = "hi"; -> strlen is 2, sizeof is 10. String functions require strings to end with a null terminator character '\0'.

rows.code: memcpy(dst, src, n) and memset(ptr, val, n)
rows.means: fast memory block copy / fills memory block with byte value
rows.consequence: memset(buf, 0, sizeof(buf)) zeroes out memory. memcpy is optimized using CPU SIMD vector registers.

rows.means: pointer literal representing memory address 0
rows.consequence: Dereferencing NULL triggers an immediate hardware segmentation fault (SIGSEGV) by the CPU memory management unit.

rows.means: program entry point receiving command-line arguments
rows.consequence: argc is the argument count; argv is an array of null-terminated string pointers (argv[0] is the program binary path).

rows.means: system error number and diagnostic printer
rows.consequence: When system calls (like open or socket) fail, they return -1 and set errno. perror prints the human-readable OS error string.

rows.means: pointer holding the memory address of an executable function
rows.consequence: Allows passing functions as callbacks to other routines, powering event loops, sorting comparators (qsort), and dynamic tables.
